public_payload.normalized_proposition: Generative AI was not in fact contributing half of US GDP growth, contrary to the White House AI advisor's claim.

statement.excerpt: Turns out it wasn’t, as Shira Ovide just reported:
statement.document_title: Turns out Generative AI was a scam

our_interpretation: Read the denial as saying the contribution was materially below approximately half, rather than merely different from exactly 50%.

Provisionally identify the target as the first half of 2025, the period identified in indexed coverage of the November statement. The underlying statement and article could not be verified through read_page.
GDP contribution means domestic output growth after accounting for imported inputs. Broad technology investment is a proxy, not a direct measurement of generative AI.
Do not substitute full-year or first-nine-month estimates for the first-half comparison.
criteria.support_condition: A credible decomposition for the referenced period isolates generative AI, or establishes a defensible upper bound, and places its contribution materially below half of US real GDP growth.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A credible decomposition for the same period and scope attributes approximately half or more of US real GDP growth to generative AI.

evidence.excerpt: Calculations conducted by Evercore ISI for the first half of 2025 produce similar results.
evidence.locator: Section 3, paragraph discussing technology investment net of imports
evidence.publisher: arXiv; Luisa Carpinelli, Filippo Natoli and Marco Taboga
evidence.explanation: The surrounding analysis reduces technology investment's growth contributions after subtracting imports and reports a similar first-half finding from Evercore. It measures broader technology activity, so it cannot directly settle the generative-AI share.

evidence.excerpt: Through the third quarter of 2025, these categories made up 39% (36% excluding data centers) of total GDP growth versus 28% in 2000.
evidence.locator: Comparison to the Dot-com Boom, final paragraph
evidence.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis
evidence.explanation: This is material evidence that related investment contributed substantially to measured growth. Its categories include non-AI activity, and its nine-month period cannot settle the first-half claim.

evidence.excerpt: In the first place, there is no established consensus for how AI investment can be identified in aggregate statistics.
evidence.locator: Appendix, limitations of the calculation methodology
evidence.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
evidence.explanation: This methodological assessment explains the attribution gap. It is not outcome evidence about first-half 2025 growth.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A readable record of the November statement, followed by a transparent, period-matched estimate or upper bound for generative AI's domestic contribution to real GDP growth.
